messages.subject: Tree with Singleton nodes (read.tree fails)
messages.subject_clean: Tree with Singleton nodes (read.tree fails)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am trying to plot trees that have singleton nodes using ggtree. I am unable to import them using read.tree because it does not support singleton nodes and cannot graph them when I read them in with read.newick, which does support singleton nodes, because it is not a valid way to read a tree in for ggtree.

I have tried using phylocom phyclean to remove the singleton nodes, but it seems to have a known bug that has not been resolved.

I have tried changing them to nexus files and reading them in, and I get the same error.

The file in question is attached.

Does anyone have any suggestions of how to get around this?

Kind regards,
Kirston

messages.subject: Re: Tree with Singleton nodes (read.tree fails)
messages.subject_clean: Tree with Singleton nodes (read.tree fails)
messages.body_plain:
This file contains tip labels like this:

'2115-DRn-24 S89 L001 R1 001 (paired).Clean.Paired.Reads sampled contig 1 consensus'

This can't be parsed as newick file, since parentheses is reserved to use in grouping nodes.

If you substitute '(paired)' to something like '_paired_', you can read the file and visualize the tree directly in ggtree.

​

messages.body_plain:

However, I have labels for the columns that are much longer than I have used before and they will not fit using the advice previously given (https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/ggtree/issues/26). I would consider changing the labels to numbers or letters and including a key elsewhere, but that would be a very sub-optimal choice given the number of columns.

Is there any way to force the object out of ggtree or gheatmap to be "taller" than it defaults to to allow longer vertical column labels to fit?

P.S. - This package is great and it is really appreciated how responsive you have been to questions/requests.

messages.subject: Is ggtree miscounting the number of edges?
messages.subject_clean: Is ggtree miscounting the number of edges?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to reproduce Example 2 in the ggtree paper with my own tree produced in PAUP and stored in nexus format. My code looks like this:

>rm(list=ls())
>library(ggtree)
>library(ape)

>tree <- read.nexus('mytree.tre')
>tree

Phylogenetic tree with 840 tips and 839 internal nodes.
Tip labels:
 A, B, C, D, E, F, ...
Rooted; includes branch lengths.
>ggtree(tree,aes(color=tree$edge.length))+
  + theme_tree2()+
  + scale_color_continuous(high='#D55E00',low='#0072B2')+geom_tiplab(size=2)

Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1679): node, parent, x, y, colour

It's is clear that ggtree is assuming there is one additional edge that doesn't exists in the tree:
>length(tree$edge.length)
[1] 1678
> nrow(tree$edge)
[1] 1678
But I can't figure out why. I've tried rerunning the code after converting the tree to Newick format and also unrooting the tree to no avail. The code runs successfully if I add one 'fictional' length (something like aes(color=c(tree$edge.length,1)),) but, since I don't know where that "1"is being landed, I'm sure I'll end up shooting myself in the foot.

I noticed also that the error message disappears if data is made explicit as in the following script, but the printed tree turns to be completely black, which is pointless

ggtree(data=tree,aes(color=edge.length))+
  theme_tree2()+
  scale_color_continuous(high='#D55E00',low='#0072B2')+geom_tiplab(size=2)

Is there an explanation for this? A bug maybe? How can I solve this issue?

Side note: get.fields also produces an error
> get.fields(tree)
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘get.fields’ for signature ‘"phylo"’

So I tried this:

library(ggtree)

tr <- rtree(30)

p1 <- ggtree(tr)
d1 <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, val=rnorm(30, sd=3))
p2 <- ggplot(d1, aes(x=id, y=val)) + geom_point() + coord_flip()
multiplot(p1 + geom_tiplab(), p2, ncol =2 )

How do I align the tip labels of the tree and the labels of the scatterplot/ or can I somehow adjust the plot size? In the example under the link, it seemed to adjust the height of the plots. Also, is it possible to sort the scatterplot according to the tip.label?

 Is there maybe a ggtree internal function for this?

Thanks in advance!e

messages.subject: Re: Is ggtree miscounting the number of edges?
messages.subject_clean: Is ggtree miscounting the number of edges?
messages.body_plain:
You are using ggtree in the wrong way.

​

For first issue, you code should be:

ggtree(tree,aes(color=branch.length))+

  theme_tree2()+
  scale_color_continuous(high='#D55E00',low='#0072B2')+geom_tiplab(size=2)

For the second issue, get.fields is S4 method for getting features available in S4 tree objects that contains tree and associated data (features).

phylo is only designed for storing tree but not with associated data, and there is no get.fields method for it.

messages.subject: Displaying Legend for Tip Labels
messages.subject_clean: Displaying Legend for Tip Labels
messages.body_plain:
I have a tree on which I have plotted bootstrap values. I also display isolation source data by color-coding the tip labels, with the end goal of mapping data using ghetmap. The source data is input via a file with the following format:
Taxon Source Color
taxon_01 Location_01 Red
taxon_02 Location_02 Blue
taxon_03 Location_02 Blue
etc.
The Source dictates the color I assigned, so in this case they are essentially equivalent. This all seems to work fine with the following code:

intermediate_tree <- ggtree(tree_file, branch.length = T,ladderize = TRUE) + geom_tiplab(size = 3, linetype = "dashed", linesize = 0.1, align = TRUE, color = tip_colors$Color) + geom_nodepoint(aes(color=bootstrap), size = 2) + geom_nodepoint(shape = 1, size = 2, color = "black") + scale_color_gradient2(midpoint = 50, low = "navyblue",mid = "ivory", high = "red1")
gheatmap(intermediate_tree,matrix_file, offset = 0.3, width = 2, colnames = F) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey","black"))

I attach a version of the result below, for reference if helpful.

My difficulty is that I would like to add a legend for the tip labels identifying that Red tips are all from location 1, etc. My use of the theme() and theme_tree() functions only seem to be able to manipulate the bootstrap legend. I attempted to follow the advice given here (https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/ggtree/issues/76)  which got me errors of (Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (46): colour, node, parent, x, y), here (http://guangchuangyu.github.io/2014/12/viewing-and-annotating-phylogenetic-tree-with-ggtree/) and (https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeAnnotation.html#the-operator) where the code:

ggtree(tree_file) %<+% tip_colors + geom_text(aes(color=tip_colors$Color, label=tip_colors$Taxon))
&
ggtree(tree_file) %<+% tip_colors + geom_tiplabt(aes(color=tip_colors$Color))  #or tip_colors$Source
returned:
Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (46): colour, label, x, y

When I strip out the bootstrap (and gheatmap) I still cannot find how to display the taxa label key.
